neighbours.label: the comma after a person's name opening a line of direct speech ("Dean, hey")
fire: She looked at her brother and sighed. "Mark, you can't stay here."
Nora ran to the door, grinning. "Tom, come and see this!"
He touched her shoulder gently. "Anna, it's going to be fine."
“Peter, we need to talk,” she whispered in the dark.
The old man turned around slowly. "Lucy, my dear, sit down."
Her mother frowned over the letter. "Kate, who sent you this?"
“Jack, put that down right now,” said the teacher.
He stood up and held out his hand. "Ben, thanks for everything."
quiet: She looked at her brother and sighed. Mark could not stay there.
Nora ran to the door, grinning. Tom came to see the puppy.
He touched her shoulder gently. Anna knew it was going to be fine.
Peter, Sarah and Paul sat talking in the dark.
The old man turned around slowly. Lucy, his daughter, sat down.
Her mother frowned over the letter that Kate, her cousin, had sent.
Jack, the teacher, put the chalk down right away.
He stood up and held out his hand. Ben, a neighbor, shook it.

short: comma after a vocative name in speech
